paper_metadata.title: Quantum Machine Learning for Anomaly Detection in Consumer Electronics

summary: The paper surveys five QML anomaly-detection case studies and reports quantitative results including 92.23%–99.34% accuracy for IoMT security assessment, 89.41% AUC on Fashion-MNIST and 88.24% on MNIST for a hybrid deep anomaly detector, 64.1% recall on a gas-turbine dataset for a 4-qubit autoencoder, and surveillance accuracies up to 100% for J-QCNN. It also reports a fraud-detection quantum-kernel model with 70% average precision and a stated 15% improvement over a classical kernel, but all evidence is hybrid/simulator-based and does not establish practical gate-based quantum advantage.

algorithm.variant: Fused semi-supervised reinforcement learning with quantum feature selection and quantum DNN

problem_instance.description: Security/vulnerability assessment on five IoMT devices: heart rate monitor, insulin pump, smart inhaler, pacemaker, and fitness tracker.

dataset_specification.description: Five devices with multiple threat types; exact split and dates not reported.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Quantum methods used to clean data and extract features before model training; exact preprocessing steps not reported.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compared against classical reinforcement learning agents, DNN, CNN, and quantum DNN; reported accuracy range across devices/threats.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Data cleaning and feature extraction; quantum feature selection (QFS) mentioned in table.

experiments.description: Quantum-classical hybrid deep anomaly detection for images using a DSVDD-inspired architecture with variational quantum layers.

experiments.description: Hybrid classical-quantum autoencoder for anomaly detection on sensor and benchmark datasets using a PQC bottleneck and isolation forest on latent features.

algorithm.variant: Hybrid Classical-Quantum Autoencoder (HAE) with isolation forest on latent space

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical encoder compresses data, then latent representation is fed into a 4-qubit PQC; measured expectation values form latent space for downstream isolation forest.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize reconstruction loss for normal data; anomalies yield high reconstruction loss and are separated in latent space.

problem_instance.description: Anomaly detection on a power plant gas turbine sensor dataset, with additional benchmarking on Musk, Arrhythmia, and Satlog datasets.
problem_instance.dataset_name: Power plant gas turbine dataset; Musk; Arrhythmia; Satlog

dataset_specification.description: Power plant dataset contains 161 sensor measurements recorded every 10 minutes over 10 months; training used one week of observations.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Original data compressed by classical encoder before quantum layer; latent space extracted and used to train isolation forest.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Reported recall for gas turbine and benchmark datasets; 30 PQC designs compared to select best HAE design.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical encoder compresses data before quantum processing.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Isolation forest trained on latent space extracted from quantum measurements.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 4-qubit PQC on a statevector simulator; reported recall is 64.1% on the gas turbine dataset, with benchmark recalls of 100% (Musk), 72.7% (Arrhythmia), and 76% (Satlog).
limiting_factors: Simulator-based evaluation, not a QPU demonstration

experiments.description: Quantum-kernel-based fraud detection using an IQP feature map and one-class SVM on credit card transactions.

algorithm.variant: Quantum kernel classifier with one-class SVM (Q-SVC / Q-OC-SVM)

hyperparameters.pca_components: first N components, where N equals number of qubits

problem_formulation.encoding_details: PCA-reduced features are encoded into an IQP circuit; N principal components are used for N qubits.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Construct a quantum kernel / Gram matrix to separate fraudulent from normal transactions using one-class SVM.

dataset_specification.description: PCA applied before quantum encoding; exact train/test split not reported.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: PCA used; first N components retained, with N equal to the number of qubits; data re-uploaded three times to increase expressivity.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compared against unsupervised kernel-based benchmark methods; average precision reported.

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Gram matrix construction and one-class SVM classification.

speedup_claims.conditions: The paper notes Gram matrix construction is O(Ns^2), new-data evaluation is O(Ns), and inference over Nd data is O(NdNs); it concludes the method is suitable only for re-checking transactions and top-priority cases, not mass real-time evaluation.
speedup_claims.caveats: No empirical runtime advantage is reported; the paper explicitly highlights scalability limitations.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(Ns^2) for Gram matrix construction; O(Ns) for new data evaluation; O(NdNs) for inference over Nd data
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(Ns^2) for kernel matrix construction; O(Ns) for new data evaluation; O(NdNs) for inference over Nd data

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Quantum-kernel fraud detection reports 70% average precision and says it outperforms the classical kernel by 15% in average precision, but the setup is simulator-based and no hardware scaling data are given.
limiting_factors: Simulator and GPU-based evaluation, not QPU hardware
